title: Basel Framework — LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio)
sourceNote: Structured rendering of the BCBS consolidated Basel Framework, standard group LCR (Liquidity Coverage Ratio, d295 lineage). Verbatim source: https://www.bis.org/basel_framework/standard/LCR.htm. Binds the bank via SARB Reg 26 and BA 325.

sections.heading: The LCR requirement
sections.text: The Liquidity Coverage Ratio promotes short-term resilience to liquidity risk by requiring a stock of unencumbered high-quality liquid assets sufficient to survive a 30 calendar-day stress scenario.

subsections.text: A bank must maintain a stock of high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) that is at least 100% of its total net cash outflows over a 30 calendar-day liquidity stress scenario. Total net cash outflows equal stressed expected cash outflows less the lesser of stressed expected cash inflows and 75% of stressed outflows.

sections.heading: HQLA composition, haircuts and cash-flow rates
sections.text: HQLA are classified into Level 1 and Level 2 (2A and 2B) assets, each subject to a haircut and composition cap; cash flows over the stress horizon are determined by prescribed run-off and inflow rates.

subsections.text: Level 1 assets are included without haircut. Level 2A assets are subject to a 15% haircut. Level 2B assets are subject to haircuts of 25% to 50%. Level 2 assets in aggregate must not exceed 40% of total HQLA, and Level 2B assets must not exceed 15% of total HQLA, both measured after haircuts.

Stressed outflow run-off rates are applied by funding category: stable retail deposits 3% to 5%; less-stable retail deposits 10%; operational wholesale deposits 25%; non-operational unsecured wholesale funding up to 100%; secured funding by collateral quality from 0% (Level 1) upward.
Total cash inflows that may be recognised are capped at 75% of total expected cash outflows, ensuring a bank holds a minimum buffer of HQLA and cannot rely entirely on inflows to meet outflows.
